description: Canonical evidence envelope schemas for CD pipeline modules. Module contracts declare `outputSchema: evidence-1`, naming the major family rather than this exact version, because a static contract cannot keep a claim about a minor that moves with the payload — the precise version travels in the envelope's own schemaVersion field. Contracts do not $ref this file, and nothing validates a runtime envelope against it. `schemaVersion` here carries a const: a pinned copy of this document therefore rejects an envelope from a newer minor, which is the signal to fetch the schema for the version the envelope names. What keeps it honest is schema_json_test.go, which fails when the property or required sets here disagree with the struct tags in schema.go. That test pins structure only: the enums, ranges and formats below are hand-authored and unenforced.

outcome.description: What a tool found, before any gate. `passed` answers a different question — "should this block?" — and under `fail-on: NONE` it answers it the same way whatever the tool saw. CLEAN: ran, found nothing. SKIPPED: did not run, legitimately — an opt-in gate left off, a selector asking for no artifact, a scanner with nothing in scope. FINDINGS: ran, reported findings at any severity. FAILED: ran, and the subject failed. ERROR: did not produce a usable result. Rolled up, SKIPPED outranks CLEAN so incomplete coverage cannot report a clean headline, and ranks below FINDINGS so a real finding still wins it. Absent means the producer has not been converted, which is a different claim from any of these.

concern.description: The question a tool answers, phrased the way the reader of a report asks it. The bundle is indexed by producing module because that is how the pipeline is built; nobody receiving a report asks it that way, and neither axis is derivable from the other — one module answers several concerns and one concern arrives from several modules. Declared by the producer, never mapped from the tool name by the aggregator: a lookup table's failure mode is silent, filing a newly added tool under whatever a fuzzy match returns while the report still reads as complete. Absent means the producer did not say, and such a row is reported as unclassified rather than dropped or guessed at.

examined.description: How much a tool actually looked at, in whatever unit it counts in — the denominator a zero finding count needs. "0 vulnerabilities" reads the same whether the scanner reached three thousand components or none. Absent means the producer did not say, which is different from count 0: a present count of 0 is the claim that the tool looked and found nothing in scope.

unit.description: What is being counted, in the producer's own words.

count.description: How many units the tool processed.

total.description: How many units existed in scope, when the tool knows. Absent when it cannot see its own denominator.

ruleSet.description: Which rules a pattern scanner applied — the second denominator a zero finding count needs. Examined says what the tool read; this says what it read it with. A pinned set that loaded fewer rules than it declares is a non-run, never a smaller clean result.

count.description: How many distinct rules the tool reported as loaded.

byLanguage.description: count split by the language directory each rule id names.

pinned.description: The fixed source the rules were held to, when there is one.

unpinned.description: Rule sources fetched at run time that nothing pins; their rules are counted but cannot be verified.

finding.description: One normalised, human-readable diagnostic behind the findingsBySeverity counts. Best-effort detail: the counts stay authoritative for the gate decision. `line` is part of a finding's identity, not decoration — without it two distinct findings in one file are byte-identical rows that deduplication collapses into one.

category.description: Descriptive rule category, not a verified vulnerability. Absent means unknown.

subcategories.description: Scanner rule context. audit and vuln are rule labels, never confirmation of an occurrence.

confidence.description: Rule-author/scanner confidence, not SARIF precision or proof of exploitability. Absent means unknown.

classificationSource.description: Origin of descriptive classification, not an independent verification.

testCounts.description: Executed-test accounting for one suite. passed + failed + skipped need not equal total: a tool that lost a result to a crash should show the gap rather than have cicd balance the books for it. durationMs is absent whenever the runner had no figure it could trust.

sourceStatus.description: One source verdict behind a combined `passed`, which is an AND across sources. The counts carry no default because an absent count and a zero count are different claims. `scope` names the fused envelope a per-tool row came from ("security-source"), and is empty in the ordinary case where the row IS the envelope.

concernRollup.description: One concern's whole answer, folded from the rows that declared it. Carries counts and a verdict, never the rows themselves: they are already in `sources`, and a second copy can disagree with the first. `tools` says how many rows stand behind the verdict without restating them. `passed` is the AND over those rows and `outcome` the worst of them, the same two folds the combined envelope uses. `examined` is summed only when every row counts in the same unit and every row states one, and is absent otherwise, because a denominator summed over the tools that answered understates the concern by whatever the silent ones looked at. `concern` is absent on the rollup covering rows whose producer declared none; those are reported, not dropped.

concernReport.description: The run seen by question rather than by module, so a consumer holding only this document can report "SAST clean, SCA failed" without knowing which module runs which scanner. Written by the aggregator only; absent on an individual module envelope, which means nobody folded it rather than no concern was answered. `notAnswered` names the concerns this run produced no rows for, and is the field that stops the list from misleading: a reader shown seven concerns cannot see that ten exist, so an absent SAST rollup would read identically to a clean one. It is not a verdict — nothing here knows which concerns a given pipeline ought to answer, and a repository with no infrastructure has no IaC leg and is not missing one.
